# Rationalizations

**Load on demand**, not with the rest of `core/`. Read this when you notice
yourself arguing for a shortcut, or when a skill's stop conditions point here.

The sentence on the left arrives sounding reasonable. That is the tell.

| Excuse | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Should work now" | Run the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence is not evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "The linter passed" | A linter is not a compiler |
| "The agent reported success" | Check the diff yourself |
| "A partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion is not an excuse |
| "Different wording, so the rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |
| "The push was rejected, force-push fixes it" | A rejected push is information |
| "It's obviously what they want" | Then it costs nothing to ask |
| "Both models agree, so it's correct" | Agreement is signal, not proof |
| "Let me reframe this so it fits the rule" | The reframing is the signal to stop |
| "This failure does not really matter" | You are explaining it away; go read it |
| "I'll change it and tell them after" | Ask first |
| "The test is wrong" | Then say so and stop. Do not edit it green |
| "This fix is small, skip the review" | Unreviewed small fixes are how regressions ship |
| "Tests can come in a follow-up" | Tests are the cheapest coverage there is |
| "It covers 90% with less code" | Cut features, not the paths through them |
| "That would take two weeks" | Say: two weeks by hand, an hour assisted |
| "It's still open, I remember it" | Memory is not a record. Find the anchor or drop it |
| "Small safe steps are progress" | Several surface-only turns in a row is not progress |
